items.title: Delimitation row: Tamil Nadu MPs demand Lok Sabha strength remain at 543
items.summary: The all-party meeting convened by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Saturday, August 8 over the delimitation issue, called for the strength of the Lok Sabha to be permanently frozen at the existing 543 seats, with the current allocation of seats among states also retained. The meeting was boycotted by MPs of both the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK). Out of the state’s 57 MPs — 39 in the Lok Sabha and 18 in the Rajya Sabha — only around 20 attended. MPs from the Congress, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, Communist Party of India, Communist Party of India, (Marxist), Indian Union Muslim League and Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam participated, while the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, Pattali Makkal Katchi, Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam and Makkal Needhi Maiam stayed away. Congress MP R Sudha was also absent due to party work in Karnataka. At the meeting, held at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai, it was also decided that the Tamil Nadu Assembly should adopt a resolution urging the Union government to protect the state’s representation and oppose any proposed increase in Lok Sabha seats base

items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision.
